title: Incident Communications: Minimum-Safe Templates + Ops Checklist (Draft)
body:
Purpose:
This working doc collects a compact set of 'minimum-safe' communications and an ops checklist for on-call SREs to use when an incident is declared. The idea is: when seconds matter, we have short, copy-pasteable messages and a simple checklist to get the war room stabilised and customers informed quickly.

Scope and assumptions:
- For P0/P1 user-impact incidents affecting hosted API or Dedicated capacity.
- Not a replacement for full Runbooks / Postmortems. This is intentionally minimal and pragmatic.
- Templates are written to be usable with minor edits (timestamps, links, short facts).
- Keep public/customer language clear + non-technical; internal comms are succinct and action-oriented.

Quick guidance (TL;DR):
- Initial internal alert within 5 mins of detection: short facts + ask to join war room.
- Status page: initial public entry within 15 mins for P0/P1 (even if provisional).
- Customer emails for large customers/outages within 30 mins (CS + comms coordinate).
- Cadence: 15m updates while unstable, move to 30/60m once mitigated.

---

1) Internal Slack / Pager message (Initial)
Channel: #sre-incidents (or ephemeral war-room channel)
Copy (paste-ready):

ALERT: Incident declared — [SHORT-TITLE]
Severity: P0/P1
Detected: [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC]
Impact: Brief one-line impact summary (e.g., "API 5xx rate increased to 18% for model endpoints in us-west1; customer requests failing")
Action: War room started at [link to call] | Join: <call-link>
Lead: @oncall-sre (incident lead) | Comms: @noah (comm lead)
Immediate ask: Please join the war room and ping if you have ownership of any affected services (model-serving, routing, cache).

Notes: attach logs/high-level metrics link (Grafana), link to current status page draft (internal), and Jira ticket if created.

---

2) War-room kickoff checklist (first 10 minutes)
- Confirm incident severity and owner (Incident Lead).
- Create/confirm incident ticket: JIRA ticket or internal incident doc with a consistent ID.
- Create a war-room channel (#war-incident-<id>) and add: Incident Lead, Comms Lead, SREs, SME (model infra, routing), CS rep, Eng on-call for impacted services.
- Share critical dashboards: error rate, latency, model queue depth, host GPU health, recent deploys.
- Identify a single source-of-truth doc and status page draft link.
- Decide short-term mitigation target (reduce error rate to < X% or failover to fallback model).
- Assign immediate tasks (eg scale pool, revert deploy, adjust routing).
- Start a timeline note in the incident doc (who did what and when).

Operational notes (war-room behaviour):
- One person posts updates to public/status page (Comms Lead) to avoid conflicting messages.
- Keep internal chatter in war-room channel; use threaded updates for ticketed actions.
- If a customer is directly impacted and flagged (VIP), assign CS rep to coordinate external outreach.

---

3) Status page template (public-facing) — INITIAL (provisional)
Title: [Service name] degraded / service disruption in [region] — investigating
Posted: [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC]
Impact: Customers may experience increased errors or latency for [API product: e.g., generation, embeddings] in [region].
Scope: Provisional — we are investigating reports from multiple customers and internal telemetry.
Current status: Investigating — We have an active incident and an engineering team working to identify root cause.
Next update: [in 15 minutes / ASAP]
Details: We will provide updates on affected endpoints, mitigation steps, and expected timeline.
Workaround: If available, provide short workaround (eg use region eu-west1, switch to fallback model id).
Contact: Support is available via support@redwood.ai for customers needing immediate assistance.

Template notes: keep it short and non-technical. If unknowns remain, state clearly "investigating" rather than guess.

---

4) Status page template — FOLLOW-UP UPDATE
Title: [Service name] — mitigation in progress / partial recovery
Updated: [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC]
Impact: Error rates have reduced from X% to Y% for [service]. Some customers may still experience intermittent failures.
What we're doing: Engineers implemented [rollback / scale up / routing change], which reduced errors. Diagnostics ongoing to determine root cause.
Next update: [in 30 minutes / in 1 hour]
Notes: If we have an ETA for full recovery, include it; if not, be transparent.

---

5) External customer email template (for impacted accounts)
Subject: Redwood — Incident affecting [service] in [region] — update
Hi [Customer name],
We want to let you know we are investigating an incident that may be affecting your [API/Model] calls in [region]. Our engineers are actively working to resolve the issue.
What we know so far:
- Impact: [short bullet: errors, increased latency, failed requests]
- When it started: [timestamp]
- What we are doing: [eg: scaling, rollback, routing to alternate region]
Expected next update: [in 30 minutes / 1 hour]. If you need urgent assistance, reply or open a ticket at [support link] and tag priority.
Thanks for your patience — we’ll keep you posted.
Regards,
[CS rep name] on behalf of Redwood SRE

Notes: personalize for VIP customers (include phone number / direct slack if offered). All external drafts must be approved by Comms Lead if available.

---

6) Internal executive status (short)
Subject: Incident brief — [SHORT-TITLE] — [P0/P1] — [start time]
One-liner: [Service] is degraded in [region]; engineering executing mitigation (rollback/scale/reroute).
Impact: High-level metrics (percent of requests failing, % customers impacted, notable customers).
Action taken: [what the team did in the last update window]
Next steps: [ETA/next update time]
Owner: [Incident Lead] | Comms: [Comms Lead]

---

7) Communication cadence & escalation rules (short)
- P0: initial update within 5–15m, public status page within 15m, customer emails to impacted VIPs within 30m. Internal cadence: 15m until degraded to 30m.
- P1: initial internal within 10–20m, status page within 60m.
- If incident exceeds 3 hours without clear mitigation, escalate to Director SRE and Product Ops.

---

8) Post-incident: immediate checklist (first 24 hours)
- Confirm service is stable and monitor for 2x mean-time-to-recover window.
- Draft preliminary internal incident summary (facts-only) and share with Product & CS.
- Schedule postmortem (RCA) within 72 hours; assign authorship.
- If customer impact was material, draft customer-facing postmortem and coordinate with CS and Legal if needed.
- Capture learnings and update runbooks / automation to prevent recurrence.

---

9) Short examples / copy to keep in pocket (one-liners)
- Internal update (join war-room): "Update T+10m: error rate increased to 16% across api-gen-1; scaling group applied +50% capacity; investigating root cause. Next update in 15m."
- Public status (short): "Investigating — We're seeing elevated errors for the generation API in us-west1 and are actively working on mitigation."
- Customer (VIP): "We’re actively working on the issue; your requests may be failing. Engineering is prioritising a rollback that should restore service in under 30 minutes. We will update you at T+30m or earlier."

---

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Do we need an automated hook that creates the status page draft from the incident ticket? (would save time; ticket: JIRA-2345)
- Clarify who owns the "public voice" during late-night incidents (Comms on-call? SRE lead?).
- Add a checklist for Dedicated customers (data isolation / private deploys) — CS play specific.
- Run a tabletop exercise with 2 SREs + 1 CS rep to validate timings.

References and links:
- Incident runbooks (Confluence): https://redwood-confluence.internal/display/SRE/Incident+Runbooks
- Incident ticket template: JIRA-INCIDENT-TEMPLATE
- Example past incident: JIRA-9876 (rollout-related degradation)

Appendix: quick copy snippets for engineers (bullet-ready)
- "Mitigation applied: scaled model pool +30% at [time]. Observed 60% reduction in queue lengths; errors decreasing."
- "Rollback started at [time]; rolling back to commit [sha]; monitoring for service stabilization."

END — this is a working document. Use freely; if you improve a phrase or cadence, update this file and ping authors.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-08: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2026-01-12: added customer email template (Noah)
